text:
Sam Ortiz: FYI — Questly reported an embeddings similarity / ordering mismatch when ranking search results. They say the same query against our embeddings endpoint + their local vectorstore yields a different ranking order consistently.

Priya Sinha: how often are they hitting this? single tenant? dedicated?

Sam Ortiz: dedicated-eu-west-1, customer says reproducible every time with 3 sample docs. Not noise — deterministic diff in ordering.

Alex Chen: can you paste minimal repro steps and sample payload? we need to triage to eng if reproducible.

Sam Ortiz: pasted repro below (Questly provided):

```
# curl to our embeddings + naive cosine ranking
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small-v2","input":["doc A text","doc B text","doc C text"]}'

# then client computes cosine similarity between query embedding and returned vectors
# Questly says their client (faiss flat index) ranks B > A > C, but our API search results for same query return A > B > C
```

Sam Ortiz: they also included a tiny vector snapshot (base64 truncated) and the query embedding. They claim reproduces 100% on their instance. Log sample from their side:

```
query_id: q-4829
scores: [0.873, 0.868, 0.621]
ids: ["A","B","C"]  # local index order by score: B(0.873) then A(0.868) then C
redwood_search_response_order: ["A","B","C"]
```

Priya Sinha: hmm. Could be tie-breaker logic, shuffling, or a post-ranking normalization step. Ask them for the exact method they use to compute scores (cosine vs dot) + whether they normalize vectors.

Sam Ortiz: asked and they replied: cosine similarity on L2-normalized vectors (faiss IndexFlatIP after normalizing). Also sent model version: text-embedding-3-small-v2 @ 2026-02-11, and call params: region eu-west, routing policy: dedicated-primary.

Alex Chen: tagging eng-runtime — @Jesse Park can you take a look? If this is a deterministic mismatch we should verify we don't apply any non-deterministic tie-breakers in search/path that affect ordering.

Jesse Park: on it. Quick questions: 1) do you have the raw float vectors (or even deterministic rounding) they used? 2) can they run a direct cosine check on embeddings returned by our endpoint vs their stored vectors?

Sam Ortiz: they sent a small CSV of vectors (float truncated to 6 decimals). Pasted a minimal pair check they ran: they computed dot(query, vecA)=0.867954 and dot(query, vecB)=0.872993 but their index reports B first. They say our API returns A first when doing a built-in /search endpoint call.

Jesse Park: OK please ask them to do two quick things and paste outputs: (A) call /embeddings with the same inputs we provide and return the raw vectors; (B) run a deterministic scorer script on those raw vectors and on their stored vectors and paste both score lists. If our returned vectors differ by rounding/quantization, that'll explain it.

Sam Ortiz: asked and they ran it. Their reply included this snippet: 

```
# scores computed on Questly side
scores_local = [0.872993, 0.867954, 0.621102]
scores_from_redwood = [0.867954, 0.868001, 0.621102]
# small difference between 1st and 2nd causes flip in final rank
```

Priya Sinha: small numeric diffs can flip ordering. Need to know if our embeddings endpoint applies any postprocessing (float16 cast, quantization, normalization) on returned vectors. Alex / Jesse?

Alex Chen: we have quantization profiles for dedicated instances. Jesse, could be a conversion to float16 for transport or a normalization step. Priority wise: P2 unless multiple customers affected. Questly seems only tenant so far.

Jesse Park: I will reproduce locally against dedicated-eu-west-1 config and run a tiny script to compare high-precision dot products. If it's a precision/transport issue we can either change rounding or document expected ordering tolerance.

triage-bot: created INF-1029 — "Questly: embeddings ordering mismatch (dedicated)" — priority P2 — assignee: eng-runtime triage queue — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1029

Sam Ortiz: added Questly sample CSV and curl traces to the ticket.

Jesse Park: quick dev repro I want to run, can you confirm this is accurate?

```
# python repro (local)
from numpy import dot
from numpy.linalg import norm
q = [...questly query floats...]
A = [...vec A floats...]
B = [...vec B floats...]
print(dot(q, A) / (norm(q)*norm(A)))
print(dot(q, B) / (norm(q)*norm(B)))
```

Jesse Park: acceptance criteria I propose before we close: 1) reproduce the ordering mismatch locally against the same model/version and dedicated config; 2) identify root cause (precision/quantization/normalization/tie-breaker); 3) either fix (prefer) or document and add a deterministic tie-breaker/regression test; 4) add unit test + integration test using Questly's sample.

Priya Sinha: +1. Also ask product if documentation/upgrade notice needed for Dedicated customers if we change transport precision. Alex?

Alex Chen: noted. I'll review release notes and decision. If it's a small fix backwards-compatible, can ship patch. If changing transport precision for dedicated instances, will coordinate with sales/CS for communication.

Sam Ortiz: marking customer notified that we've opened INF-1029 and eng will investigate. They asked for ETA; I told them we'll triage within 48 hours and provide a follow-up.

Jesse Park: starting local repro now. I'll update the ticket and tag back here once I have a root cause.

Priya Sinha: thanks team. Sam — keep Questly updated with milestones. 

Sam Ortiz: will do :thumbsup:
